reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a quasi-periodic oscillation with a fundamental period of ~16 points, evident across all candidates when scaled to cycle count (1P, 3P, 3P, 5P). Each cycle exhibits a characteristic asymmetric sawtooth-like shape: a relatively slow, smooth descent (~8–10 points) from a rounded peak to a sharp, steep trough (~2–3 points), followed by a rapid, near-linear ascent (~4–6 points) back toward the next peak. Peaks are broad and plateau-like (duration 2–4 points), typically at robust-standardized values between -0.2 and +1.0; troughs are narrow and sharp, consistently near -1.4 to -1.5. Baseline level varies modestly across segments (median range: -0.27 to +0.20), but morphology remains stable—roughness (~0.202) and curvature (~0.07–0.13) are tightly clustered. Noise is low and structured: minor high-frequency jitter is absent; deviations are smooth and deterministic, suggesting underlying dynamics rather than stochastic noise. Amplitude (90th percentile) ranges 2.07–3.17, with candidate 2 showing higher amplitude due to elevated peak levels, not structural change. No sustained trend is present within windows; slope per point is near-zero (±0.05), confirming stationarity. Acceptable variation includes moderate baseline shifts and peak height modulation, but the descent-then-ascent motif, trough sharpness, and cycle symmetry must be preserved.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle (1P) segment showing one full asymmetric oscillation: gentle descent from ~−0.5 to −1.4 over 5 points, sharp trough at index 5, then steep linear rise to plateau near +0.9 for 3 points, followed by gradual decay. Minimal noise; clean boundaries with no truncation artifacts.

Three-cycle (3P) segment with consistent repetition of the core motif: three identical descent–trough–ascent patterns. Troughs align near −1.5, peaks plateau near +0.5–0.6. Minor baseline drift negligible; slight asymmetry in second cycle’s ascent is within expected variation. No anomalies detected.

Three-cycle (3P) segment with higher-amplitude peaks (~+2.0) but preserved morphology: same descent–sharp-trough–ascent sequence. Peak plateaus slightly longer; troughs remain sharp and deep (−1.4 to −1.5). Slight baseline elevation (+0.2 median) explains amplitude increase; no structural deviation.

Five-cycle (5P) segment showing robust periodicity over extended context. All five cycles replicate the motif faithfully; troughs consistently at −1.5, peaks at ~+0.5–1.0 with brief plateaus. Minor cycle-to-cycle amplitude modulation acceptable; no trend or distortion. Boundary truncation absent; full cycles intact.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 3 (5P) for queries ≥5 cycles due to highest statistical reliability and full-context validation. For 1–2 cycle queries, use reference 0 (1P) for precise motif anchoring. For 3-cycle queries, prefer reference 1 over 2 when baseline is near zero; use reference 2 only if query shows elevated peaks without morphological change. Always prioritize trough sharpness and descent/ascent asymmetry over absolute amplitude or baseline level.
